decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right, pens on the left. Begin right inward side-grasp orientation with small elbow-up continuous increments; left waits.
Advance the right hand toward the holder from its right side, leveling the side grasp. Keep left clear; refine approach from wrist view.
Refine the right side approach: holder is forward and slightly inward of the open fingers. Move slowly to cup mid-height.
Cup has tilted during approach. Withdraw slightly outward and reposition forward with fingers open to clear contact and reassess before grasping.
Reapproach the fallen holder at its new lower center with open fingers; use slow visual alignment before attempting to recover it.
Shift inward to enclose the fallen holder without pushing downward, close the right gripper, then inspect before lifting.
Lift the closed right gripper slowly and retreat from the far edge, checking whether the holder is retained before righting it.
Holder remained on the table. Open and change to an overhead recovery grasp, keeping clearance and approaching only from the right workspace.
Prior action was rejected without motion. Retry the overhead transition with quarter-sized rotational increments and small translation.
Continue overhead recovery alignment above the fallen holder, turning the jaws across its width while remaining clear of the table.
Center the right wrist above the holder and finish pointing fingers downward for a width grasp; no closure until visually aligned.
After the continuity stop, retain the accepted wrist angle and translate toward the holder center with smaller increments, avoiding further elbow folding.
Set the open jaws slightly lower around the holder width, close fully, and perform a short lift to test retention from the images.
Holder appears enclosed. Lift and retreat to gain clearance, starting a gentle righting rotation; verify which end is open from the next view.
The holder was not retained. Reopen and realign over its shifted center with the jaws across its width; approach lower before closing.
Lower the open jaws around the holder rather than above it, then close without lifting so the grasp can settle.
Maintain closure, then make a small vertical test lift without rotation to verify holder retention.
The fingers closed above the holder. Reopen and descend farther while keeping the width alignment, stopping before another closure to inspect depth.
Lower another two centimeters to engage the sides, close and settle, then test with a short straight lift.
Maintain the closed grasp and lift without changing orientation, checking that the holder follows rather than staying on the table.
Holder follows the hand. Raise for clearance and rotate it partway upright, maintaining full closure and inspecting the opening direction.
Continue righting the retained holder and level its long axis, shifting the right wrist outward to leave room for the left hand.
Holder opening is visible. Level and lower it to an accessible support height while beginning the left overhead approach to the cyan pen.
Hold the now-upright cup still. Align the left open gripper downward and along the cyan pen near its capped end, keeping approach clearance.
Correct the left wrist laterally toward the cyan pen and finish the downward orientation, descending gradually with jaws open. Right keeps the cup upright.
Use the close wrist view to correct the cyan pen toward the gap between the fingers, moving laterally and toward its cap without descending further.
The previous lateral correction moved the pen away from center. Reverse that direction and advance the open left jaws across its width; maintain height and cup support.
Cyan pen is now between the open jaws. Shift along it toward the cap and square the jaw alignment while lowering slowly to grasp height.
Make the final small centering adjustment on the cyan pen, close the left gripper, and test retention with a short vertical lift. Keep the holder steady.
Cyan pen is retained between the jaws. Raise it clear of the table and begin rotating its capped end upward; right hand continues supporting the upright holder.
Bring the retained cyan pen upright and toward the holder from the left, maintaining vertical clearance and keeping the two wrists on their own sides.
Replan after the continuity guard with smaller wrist rotation. Raise the upright cyan pen above the rim while advancing toward the opening.
The cyan pen is above the opening. Make a small forward/inward correction and begin a slow insertion, retaining both grasps.
Cyan pen is centered over the mouth. Lower straight into the upright holder slowly, watching for rim contact before releasing.
Seat the cyan pen a little farther, release it inside the holder, then withdraw the left fingers upward and leftward while the right hand stays closed.
Cyan remains in the supported holder. Move the open left hand toward the purple pen and begin an overhead grasp orientation, leaving the filled holder steady.
Continue the left overhead approach toward the purple pen, compensating wrist position as the fingers turn downward. Keep a clear gap above the tabletop.
After the continuity stop, keep the accepted orientation and use smaller translations to center the purple pen between the open fingers and lower toward it.
Continue visually centering on the purple pen, move along it toward the cap and make a small yaw correction while approaching grasp height.
Replan from the accepted pose after the IK stop. Avoid further forward reach and rotation; lower while making a small width-centering correction for a nearer grasp on the purple pen.
Purple is centered at grasp depth. Close without further descent, then lift while retreating to preserve elbow continuity and verify retention.
Purple is retained. Lift and retreat from the far reach while rotating its capped end upward; keep the supported holder steady.
Finish turning the purple pen upright and raise its lower end above the rim, approaching the empty left side of the holder.
Purple is near the left lip. Lift slightly to clear the rim, correct toward the mouth, and lower cautiously without pressing the holder.
Lower the purple pen into the open left portion of the holder, release without pushing the rim, and withdraw slightly to inspect retention.
Two pens remain in the holder. Withdraw toward the black-and-gold pen and begin turning the left open gripper downward for its pickup.
Approach the black-and-gold pen from above with the left arm, lowering gradually as the fingers rotate downward; keep both inserted pens supported.
Correct across the black-and-gold pen toward the open finger gap, finish the downward alignment, and descend slowly while preserving the elbow-up branch.
Center the nearer shaft of the black-and-gold pen and lower to grasp depth, then close and settle without further forward reach.
Lift the black-and-gold pen with the left gripper closed and retreat from the far reach while beginning the upright rotation; check retention visually.
Black-and-gold pen is retained. Finish rotating it upright and carry it above the holder from the left, leaving clearance for the existing pens.
After the continuity interruption, use smaller rotations to finish upright alignment. Raise the lower end above the rim and translate toward the empty left portion of the holder.
Lower the black-and-gold pen into the left side of the opening with only a tiny inward correction; keep both grasps closed until the lower end is inside.
Release the black-and-gold pen at the opening without further downward pressure, then withdraw upward and leftward. Keep the holder securely supported.

The black-and-gold pen fell outside the holder; it will need recovery. Move the left hand clear and begin the overhead approach to the remaining white pen while keeping the two inserted pens supported.
Continue the white pen approach with open jaws, turning downward along its length and lowering above its capped end; leave the right arm steady.
The white pen is aligned across the jaws but its cap is beyond the wrist view. Move forward along the shaft and lower to grasp height with a small centering correction.
Make a final small lateral and yaw correction around the white pen, close at shaft height, and test the grasp with a short lift.
White pen is retained. Lift clear and retreat while smoothly rotating it toward cap-up, keeping the holder supported and avoiding the far-reach configuration.
Continue raising the retained white pen and turning it upright while moving toward the holder from the left; keep clear of the inserted pens.
Finish bringing the white pen upright and lift its lower end clear of the lip, approaching the open left side without releasing yet.
Lower the white pen slowly into the empty left portion of the mouth while maintaining closure; inspect penetration before release.

Seat the white pen a little farther, release it inside, and withdraw left/up. The dropped black-and-gold pen is on the right, so a support-hand change may be needed to recover it without crossing arms.

Three pens appear retained. Bring the open left hand down beside the holder for a support handoff, keeping the right grasp closed so the right arm can later retrieve the dropped pen in its own workspace.
Advance the open left fingers around the holder's left side at mid-height for a cautious handoff; the right hand maintains its grasp.
Close the left fingers around the holder and allow the shared grasp to settle without further inward pressure. Keep the right hand closed until the transfer can be checked.
Transfer support to the closed left hand: open the right fingers first, then withdraw them outward a short distance while checking that the upright holder remains with the left hand.
The handoff did not retain the holder, but it landed upright with three pens. Reopen the left fingers and approach its lower body on the table for a secure regrasp; right stays clear.
Enclose the holder a little deeper at body height with the left fingers, then close and settle without lifting or pushing farther.
The holder tilted during closure. Reopen and lower the left fingers slightly around its base, approaching a little deeper while keeping the wrist on the left side. Inspect before closing again.
The holder has shifted and tipped toward the front. Clear the left hand and bring the right hand above it for a width grasp, avoiding further side pushing while the pens remain partly contained.
Keep the left arm clear and position the right open jaws above the fallen holder, rotating toward a top-down width grasp without contacting the protruding pens.
Bring the right wrist over the holder's body and finish the downward width alignment with open fingers. Keep the protruding pens undisturbed and inspect before closing.
Center the holder body between the right fingers using the wrist view, complete the downward alignment, and lower gradually for a width grasp away from the pens.
The holder body is now between the open right jaws. Lower slightly, close around its sides, and test with a small straight lift before attempting to right it.
The holder appears enclosed. Lift with the right gripper closed and rotate its forward-facing mouth upward, keeping the left arm clear and watching whether the pens stay contained.
